warning_message: This artwork contains flashing lights that may trigger seizures in people with photosensitive epilepsy.
artwork_paragraph_1: Conceived in 2010, this work takes the form of an audiovisual piece that is both imposing and immersive. Precise, repetitive sounds are translated into binary sequences and represented by barcodes that scroll by at an extremely high speed.
artwork_paragraph_2: The speed of the projections challenges human perception and creates a sense of vibration and continuous movement.
artwork_paragraph_3: The work thus establishes a link between data, technology and perception, by reducing complex information to its most basic form: binary code.
other_works_intro: Aside from the installations, the ‘test pattern’ project also exists in several more unique forms.
other_works_cd: The album Test Pattern, released in 2008, features 16 electronic tracks totalling nearly an hour in length, built around binary sequences.
other_works_book: The book Test Pattern, published in 2017, brings the series’ aesthetic to the page: 150 pages of black-and-white barcodes.
author_paragraph_1: Born in 1966 in Gifu, Ryōji Ikeda is a Japanese composer of electronic music and a visual artist.
author_paragraph_2: To create these environments, designed to fully immerse the viewer, he combines a visual aesthetic with a precise soundscape.
author_paragraph_3: His music consists of pure sine waves, white noise, clicks, glitch sounds and frequencies close to the limit of human hearing.
author_paragraph_4: He is known for making visible the information contained within computer systems that is normally invisible. This approach thus places the work at the crossroads of minimalism, digital art and data art.
author_paragraph_5: But Ryōji Ikeda is not the only person behind this work: it is the programmer Tomonaga Tokuyama who writes the complex algorithms capable of translating and bringing to life Ryōji Ikeda’s vision.
minimalism_paragraph_1: Minimalism, which emerged in the United States during the 1960s, is characterised by a desire to minimise the use of form and colour.
minimalism_paragraph_2: Contrary to what one might think, it does not aim for simplicity in the basic sense, but rather for economy of means and a rejection of figuration.
minimalism_paragraph_3: Even today, this art form continues to exert a major influence on contemporary art.
digital_art_paragraph_1: Digital art first emerged in the 1950s and 1960s, when the first computers appeared.
digital_art_paragraph_2: Digital art encompasses a wide range of artistic practices that use digital technologies as an integral part of the creative process, with the aim of creating visual, audio or interactive works.
data_art_paragraph_1: Data Art has its origins in 1970, when the MoMA in New York opened Kynaston McShine’s exhibition ‘Information’. It is an art movement that uses raw data for artistic purposes.
